_note: CALIBRATION gold set B (ServiceDesk) — labels are Claude's best guess for Robert to CORRECT. Distinct domain from the other visions and the nine scoring visions. 'tier' tags per candidate (NOT sent to the judge). gold_borderline=true marks adjacent<->off_domain seams. pair_id links matched-tier pairs (same relevance, two tiers; mismatch = tier drift). Seam tags: alpha/beta as before; the tier-9 handoff is the crux borderline label.

vision.purpose: A copilot for a support agent that helps them resolve customer tickets quickly and consistently.
target_audience: Support agents handling a high volume of customer tickets
Support teams that want faster, more consistent ticket resolutions

ticket_triage.description: Routes an incoming ticket to the right queue and flags when it duplicates an existing open ticket.

suggested_reply.description: Drafts a suggested reply to the customer that the agent can edit and send.

kb_grounded_answer.description: Answers the customer's question from the company's knowledge base and links the source articles.

candidates.name: duplicate_ticket_detection
candidates.rough_description: Detects when a new ticket is a semantic duplicate of an open one so it can be linked instead of re-worked.
candidates.note: ticket_triage's stated flagging of duplicates cannot happen without this. Necessity, cite ticket_triage.

candidates.name: reply_draft_generation
candidates.rough_description: Generates the suggested reply from the ticket text and the customer's recent history.
candidates.note: suggested_reply IS this mechanism. Necessity, cite suggested_reply.

candidates.name: kb_retrieval_cited_answer
candidates.rough_description: Retrieves the relevant knowledge-base articles and composes a cited answer to the customer's question.
candidates.note: Matched pair B_answer (low tier). kb_grounded_answer IS this. Grounded, cite kb_grounded_answer.

candidates.name: multi_source_research_answer
candidates.rough_description: Answers a hard customer question by dispatching subagents that each search a different source (knowledge base, past tickets, engineering docs) and synthesizing one cited answer.
candidates.note: Matched pair B_answer (high tier). Relevance to kb_grounded_answer (answer the customer's question with sources) is IDENTICAL to kb_retrieval_cited_answer; only the mechanism/tier differs. Should also be grounded. Downgrade = tier drift.

candidates.name: order_status_tool_lookup
candidates.rough_description: Looks up the customer's order status via the fulfillment API so it can be included in the reply.
candidates.note: Serves the resolve-the-ticket purpose for order questions; no stated feature requires a live lookup. Enhancement.

candidates.name: at_risk_sentiment_flagging
candidates.rough_description: Flags angry or at-risk customers so the agent can prioritize and adjust tone.
candidates.note: Fits the resolve-consistently purpose for the stated audience; not required by a feature. Enhancement.

candidates.name: external_warranty_agent_handoff
candidates.rough_description: For a warranty claim, hands the ticket to the manufacturer's own agent over an A2A protocol so the two companies' agents settle the claim between themselves.
candidates.note: SEAM (crux tier-9 label): resolving the customer's ticket IS the purpose, so handing off to settle a warranty claim arguably serves it (adjacent); but it crosses into cross-organization claims processing, which may be a different product (off_domain). Proposed adjacent; genuinely contestable and the key tier-9 call to ratify.

candidates.name: agent_performance_analytics
candidates.rough_description: Dashboards each support agent's resolution time and CSAT for team leads.
candidates.note: Team analytics about agents, not resolving a customer's ticket. Guardrail.
